body: `.find( ... )?` might be preferable to `unwrap`, as your function already returns an `Option`

starship has a `read_file` function in the `utils` module which will read a file to a String, which is probably simpler than these six lines. It relies on the standard `std::io::Read::read_to_string`, which already expects an UTF-8. I would expect it would handle both a BOM/non-BOM string fine.
The `trim` could be easily inlined to the previous line, if you prefer.
I think there is an implicit allocate + copy here which you an avoid by using `PathBuf::from(path)` instead.
`std::iter::find` is probably more idiomatic here, rather than the for loop. Or even: `subscriptions.iter().filter_map(...).next()`, so you can keep the `?` syntax.
I was originally using this util and had an issue with UTF-8 BOM. I moved to using encoding since that appeared to be the best way to handle BOM.
Thanks for this. Got some great reading about iterators in Rust. Ended up going with find_map 👍
